seo.title: ODDfest 2027 — Helsinki's creative week
seo.description: ODDfest 2027 is Helsinki's creative week: independently made events across the city, bringing cultural and creative scenes together in one shared programme.

heroMedia.sub: Helsinki's creative week, bringing cultural and creative scenes together.

whatItIs.headline: One shared week, made by Helsinki's creative communities.
whatItIs.body:
ODDfest is a week of independently made events across Helsinki. Artists, collectives, venues, organisations, communities and companies make and produce their own. Bring what you do best — ODDfest gives it a place in a bigger shared week.

On its own, an event reaches its own audience. Brought together with many others across one week, it becomes part of a bigger citywide moment — connecting different scenes, audiences and ideas that might not otherwise meet.

ownership.headline: Your event. One shared week.

host.title: You bring the idea.
host.body: Create the event, experience or programme you want to make, in your own way.

odd.title: ODD brings the week together.
odd.body: We build the shared identity, programme, communications, PR and map around the week — and help connect hosts with venues, partners and each other where useful.

ownership.closing: ODDfest doesn't produce the events for you. It brings independently made events together so they're easier to discover, reach wider audiences and become part of one bigger citywide week.
ownership.stepsLabel: From an idea to the programme

howItWorks.title: Start with what you do best
howItWorks.body: An exhibition, a performance, a workshop, a screening, a dinner, an open studio, a club night, a conversation — or a format nobody has tried yet. If it belongs in Helsinki's creative life, it belongs in the week.

howItWorks.title: Tell us about it
howItWorks.body: It does not have to be finished, funded or scheduled. We want to know what you are making, roughly where and when it could happen, how far along it is, and whether there is anything you are still looking for.

howItWorks.title: Build it your way
howItWorks.body: You shape and produce your event. Where useful, we can help connect you with other hosts, venues, partners or resources. Tell us what would make the biggest difference and we'll be clear about what we can help with.

howItWorks.title: Join the shared week
howItWorks.body: Your event is connected to the ODDfest identity, the public programme and the communications around the week. For a few days, independent work across Helsinki becomes easier to find as one whole.

join.headline: Bring something to ODDfest 2027.
join.body: We are collecting event ideas now, before the dates are fixed — which is the best moment to bring one. Tell us what you want to make happen, where you are with it, and what kind of connections or support would actually be useful.
join.reassurance: An idea still at the notes-on-your-phone stage is a fine thing to send. Sending it commits you to nothing, and we would far rather hear it early than hear it finished and too late.

examplesIntro.headline: One week. Many hosts.
examplesIntro.body: In 2026, Creative Week brought more than 1,000 people to partner events across Helsinki, while ODDfest brought more than 150 acts to five venues. A few highlights from both — each one made with someone else.
examplesIntro.closing: The point is not that these events look alike. It is that, for one week, they become easier to discover together.

examples.title: ODDtheatre
examples.body: Club Theatre took over the main hall: dancers, DJs, actors, models and visual artists building one night in real time, directed by Tyre. Among them the House of Xclusive Lanvin, contemporary circus group Nuua, Wanda O'rly and Maryisonacid.

examples.title: Creative x Tech: Ecosystem Convergence
examples.body: Founders, artists, hackers, designers, musicians and cultural operators in one room — people who usually build in separate circles. Talks, fireside chats and participatory programme opened the week.

examples.title: Smell the Art
examples.host: With Helsinki Perfume Club and Artishok.me
examples.body: An exhibition for two senses: artworks paired with chosen fragrances, so scent could deepen, disrupt or extend what the eye saw. Created by Katia Los and Adriana Knispel.

examples.title: Soirée of Serendipity
examples.host: Curated by Vivian White Futures Studio
examples.body: An invitation-only evening on the soul of tomorrow — what a good life in the future is made of. Around 300 leaders, entrepreneurs, artists and thinkers from business, culture and society.

examples.title: Decoration, product or societal structure?
examples.host: With Hanaholmen and Nordic Culture Point
examples.body: A public panel, in Swedish, on where culture's value lies as funding tightens — with voices from the Kordelin Foundation, Kulturanalys Norden, Way Out West and Espoo Theatre.

examples.title: ODDgames
examples.host: With Espoo Game LAB, Odd Latent and Super Bario
examples.body: ODDgames transformed Tavastia into a multi-layered playground where games, creativity and new technology came together. Across two days, visitors explored indie games from Espoo Game LAB, experimented with AI-assisted vibe coding, experienced live game-making and creative sessions, and played together at Super Bario.

examples.title: Creative Capital Gathering
examples.host: With FiBAN and Joy for Innovation
examples.body: Investors, foundations, funds and angels around one question: what does it really mean to invest in the creative industries? A conversation rather than a pitch session, with Solar Films founder Markus Selin and a Meow Wolf case among the speakers.

examples.title: ODD Deep Space
examples.body: ODD Deep Space transformed Kamppi Chapel into a dreamlike satellite where body, mind and urgent questions about the future came together through movement, sound and experimental formats. Across two days, visitors explored themes from work, wellbeing and money to AI, planetary limits and feminist futures, guided by artist and somatic facilitator Simo Vassinen and a diverse group of thinkers, movers and makers.

hostCta.headline: Want your event in the next one?
hostCta.body: An exhibition, a club night, a talk, a dinner, an open studio — or a format nobody has tried yet. We are collecting ideas for 2027 now, and yours does not need to be finished.

faq.question: Do I need to be an established organisation to host something?
faq.answer: No. Artists, collectives, venues, companies, communities and people with no organisation behind them at all are all welcome to host. There is no track record you need to have and no size you need to be.

faq.question: Is my event too small or too niche?
faq.answer: There is no minimum. A week made only of large events would miss the point of it. A one-room exhibition, a listening session for twenty people, or a workshop in your own studio are all the right size.

faq.question: Does taking part cost anything?
faq.answer: The 2027 participation model is still being finalised. Before any host is asked to commit, we will publish clearly what is charged, if anything, what is included, and how any shared commercial arrangement works. Hosts keep control of their own event economics unless a separate agreement says otherwise.

faq.question: Can my event be free, or ticketed?
faq.answer: Either. Hosts control their own ticketing unless a specific collaboration agreement says otherwise. There is no single central ODDfest ticket covering the distributed programme.

faq.question: What if I don't have a space yet?
faq.answer: Tell us anyway. Events can happen in venues, studios, galleries, offices and public spaces across Helsinki. We cannot promise to find you a room, but if there is a match among other hosts, venues or partners we will make the introduction — and we would rather know what you are looking for early than hear about it too late.

faq.question: What if my event is happening anyway, with or without ODDfest?
faq.answer: Then it is a good candidate. Joining the week does not change what your event is. It connects something already happening to a moment when more people are looking.

faq.question: Will anyone actually come?
faq.answer: We cannot promise you an audience, and we would not trust anyone who did. What the week does is put your event into one programme alongside everything else happening those days, and spend the week telling people the whole thing is on — so your event is not the only reason someone has to be out that night.

faq.question: When is ODDfest 2027?
faq.answer: The exact dates are not confirmed yet. Send your idea anyway — nothing is lost by being early, and we will share the dates as soon as they are set.

faq.question: Is ODDference part of ODDfest?
faq.answer: They are separate things that share a week. ODDference is ODD's own professional event, about what business and the rest of society can learn from creative expertise. It is produced centrally by ODD and has its own ticket. ODDfest is the open week made by its hosts.

faq.question: I just want to attend — how does that work?
faq.answer: Once the programme is published, every event carries its own time, place and ticketing information. You choose what you want to see across the week.

partnerCta.title: Partner with ODDfest
partnerCta.body: A week made by hundreds of people needs partners behind it — organisations that want to back the week itself, reach the people in it, or build something of their own inside it. Tell us what you have in mind and we will work out whether there is a real fit.
